task: T1 pilot result recomputation with fixed positive-control predicate
what_went_wrong: positive_control() bounded predicate used est[0]*3 (=33 tokens) as the bound for a ~2048-token cap — impossible by construction, producing a false 'UNEXPECTED (cap set but grew like verbatim)' verdict for the correctly-bounded C-win arm at h=100 and h=250.

Recompute attempt launched run_pilot.py with relative default results_dir while shell cwd was 'Agentic Layer', creating a bogus duplicate results tree at 'Agentic Layer/results/pilot' and re-running h10/h25/P_h50 (~$0.04, 9 API runs wasted).
finalize() aggregates only the results list from the current invocation (re-run subset); a mixed skip/re-run resume would have written an incomplete summary.json.
root_cause: bounded-check predicate written against est[0] (first hop, tiny) instead of the configured cap constant.
Default results_dir resolved against shell cwd instead of the script directory; finalize() had no defense against partial result sets.
what_i_actually_did_wrong: Launched a recompute in a shell with a different cwd without checking that run_pilot's default results_dir is relative; did not audit the positive_control predicate when writing it (accepted an impossible bound).
detection: Flagged 'UNEXPECTED' control verdict triggered manual verification of actual est sequences; suspicious re-run log lines revealed the duplicate tree.
fix_applied: runner.py positive_control(): bounded = (not grew) or est[-1] <= cap*1.02 using WINDOW/COMPACTION_TOKENS constant.
run_pilot.py: BASE anchored to script dir, _rd() normalizes all results dirs; skip branch now loads completed results via new runner.load_result() so finalize() always aggregates the full matrix.
Deleted bogus 'Agentic Layer/results/pilot'; rebuilt pilot summary offline (zero API calls) — all 4 cap-exercised controls now OK.
